1. (Currently Amended) A method of cementing comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin processed from a source other than Barlet-Gouedard et al.; and allowing the cement composition to set.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 3 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed, wherein the viscosity is maintained for at least 4 hours.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein a suspension aid is not added to the cement composition and the composition is free of hydrocolloids.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 1 wt.% of the cement composition.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 700 or higher.

7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises a carboxymethylated inulin that exhibits enhanced properties compared to conventional inulin.

8. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 7 wherein the carboxymethylated inulin has a degree of substitution by carboxymethyl of from about 0.2 to about 0.4.

9. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.5 to about 5 wt.% of carboxylated inulin.

10. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acid with a specific lipid profile, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination thereof.

11. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a subterranean formation that has not been previously treated with other cement compositions.

12. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore with specific dimensional constraints.

13. (Currently Amended) A method of cementing in a subterranean formation comprising: providing a cement composition comprising a carboxylated inulin processed from a source other than Barlet-Gouedard et al.; placing the cement composition in the subterranean formation; and allowing the cement composition to set therein.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a thickening time of from about 3 hours to about 11 hours at temperatures up to about 280 *F.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein a viscosity of the cement composition is about constant for a period of time after the cement composition is placed, wherein the viscosity is maintained for at least 4 hours.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein a suspension aid is not added to the cement composition and the composition is free of hydrocolloids.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition has a free water separation of from about 0.0 to about 1 wt.% of the cement composition.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin is derived from an inulin having an average molecular weight of about 700 or higher.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the carboxylated inulin comprises a carboxymethylated inulin that exhibits enhanced properties compared to conventional inulin.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 19 wherein the carboxymethylated inulin has a degree of substitution by carboxymethyl of from about 0.2 to about 0.4.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition comprises from about 0.5 to about 5 wt.% of carboxylated inulin.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition further comprises borate salts, an organic acid comprising an alpha-hydroxycarboxylic acid with a specific lipid profile, a synthetic polymer comprising a carboxylate group, or any combination thereof.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the cement composition is placed in a wellbore with specific dimensional constraints.

### The remaining claims (24-42) are hereby cancelled.
